name: Quake II — leak test (experimental)
summary: Experimental: only the Quake II compile step, with the leak test on: does the map leak, and where.
description:
For the question “is this map sealed”, asked of one exact saved revision of a Quake II map. It runs qbsp in its Quake II mode with `-leaktest` and stops there: no visibility, no lighting, no package and no engine, because none of them says anything about a leak.

Measured on the Auto-Pigeon build of ericw-tools, release 1.4518 (`Q2_010`), with authored controls: a leaked map exits 1, prints `Reached occupant … at (x y z)` and `Leak file written`, writes `level.pts` and `level.leak.prt` and no BSP. The compile step is therefore recorded as failed — its BSP is not there, which is the truthful state of a compile that refused to write one — while the leak is a separate fact, read from what qbsp printed and the point file it left. Both are published: the point file as `pts`, and everything qbsp printed as `compile_log`, whichever way the step ended. qbsp's own `.log` file is not that text: it leaves out the stage headings, the fill report among them.

The point file runs from the entity qbsp reached — its origin is the one the log names — to outside the map, like Quake 1's and unlike Quake III's.

What a pass means is narrow on purpose: this compiler, at this version, found no leak in this revision, every texture the map names was found, and the BSP it wrote is a Quake II one (`IBSP:38`). A map with no entity standing in open space — none at all, or every one inside a brush — is not tested: qbsp says `No entities in empty space`, floods nothing and still writes a BSP and exits 0, and that is reported as not tested. A detail brush, a clip brush or a translucent window across a gap does not seal it. A wall naming a texture qbsp could not open is a face whose contents nobody read, so a room it closes is not called sealed.

This pipeline names the family's default Quake II tool. Only release 1.4518 of the Auto-Pigeon build has been measured: with any other qbsp a leak it reports is still a leak, and nothing else is a verdict. To run it with the Auto-Pigeon build, make your own copy of this pipeline whose stage names that tool, and choose it as the Quake II leak test.

The Auto-Pigeon editor asks for this pipeline through an `autopigeon://leaktest/` link, and a person approves it here before anything runs.

Quake II support in Auto-Pigeon is work in progress. Some textures, entities, compilation and engine workflows may be incomplete.
